comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1, C2, C60-C63, C73. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed quantitative analysis with caution about the 20% improvement claim varying by subgroup. Peer reviewers describe results as 'quite convincing' with 'modest average accuracy gain' acknowledged.

Perfect agreement on claims C27-C35, C38-C39 regarding AF2 benchmarking. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides comprehensive analysis across multiple metrics on two datasets, concluding AF2 is effective for overall structure but comparable for CDR-H3. Peer reviewers accept these benchmarking results as 'quite convincing' comparative analysis.

Perfect agreement on claims C3, C64-C65 regarding experimental validation. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes limitation of only 3 structures from single antibody family and that high AF2 confidence meant validation primarily confirms AF2. Peer reviewers explicitly praise experimental validation as a strength without noting these limitations.

Perfect agreement on claims C58-C59 regarding PLM selection and fine-tuning. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval raises concerns about lack of fine-tuning details, overfitting controls, and statistical significance of modest improvements. Peer reviewers accept this as part of 'clearly described' experimental design without questioning these methodological details.

Perfect agreement on claims C66-C68 regarding surface property predictions. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are derivative metrics dependent on structural accuracy and questions biological significance of small differences. Peer reviewers emphasize benefits for 'drug discovery and therapeutic design' without addressing these concerns.

Agreement on claims C69-C71 regarding binding predictions, but different evaluation types. OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN due to methodological concerns (superimposition rather than de novo prediction, MM/GBSA limitations, lack of experimental validation). Peer reviewers evaluate as SUPPORTED, emphasizing relevance for therapeutic applications without addressing methodological limitations.

Agreement on claim C77 regarding CAMEO 2022 validation, but different evaluation types. OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN due to very small sample size (n=7) and substantial variability. Peer reviewers evaluate as SUPPORTED as part of 'quite convincing' validation strategy without noting sample size limitations.

Perfect agreement on claims C79-C83 regarding length-dependent performance. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes mechanistic explanation about ESM2 fine-tuning is speculative. Peer reviewers acknowledge improvements for easy cases and comparable performance for challenging cases, reflecting 'methodological limit in the field.'

Agreement on claims C4-C5, C92-C93 regarding applications, but different evaluation types. OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are forward-looking statements without direct evidence of successful antibody optimization. Peer reviewers evaluate as SUPPORTED, emphasizing method can 'aid in the design of antibodies' for research and industrial applications.

Agreement on claims C78, C84, C86 regarding future directions, but different evaluation types. OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative hypotheses, with C86 contradicting demonstrated failure of physics-based approaches. Peer reviewers evaluate as SUPPORTED as reasonable future directions, noting framework 'can be easily adapted and improved.'

Strong agreement on claims C40-C43 regarding QM refinement negative results. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval praises rigorous reporting of negative results while noting small initial test set (n=14). Peer reviewers accept transparent presentation of negative results as part of rationale for PLM-based approach. OpenEval also addresses C85 which peer review groups with MD results.

Strong agreement on claims C44-C46 regarding MD refinement negative results. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses C44-C46 and praises honest reporting of failed optimization. Peer reviewers address C44-C46 plus C85, accepting negative results as supporting rationale for chosen approach. Both recognize transparent presentation of methodological exploration.

Strong agreement on claims C50-C57 regarding method architecture and ablation studies. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of component contributions but notes confidence threshold (0.8) lacks cross-validation justification. Peer reviewers praise framework as 'novel' and 'clearly described' without questioning threshold selection. OpenEval also addresses C47-C49 and C53 not in peer R4.

Partial overlap on claims C47-C49 regarding dataset and experimental design. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses broader set (C47-C57) including ablation studies with concerns about confidence threshold. Peer reviewers focus on dataset compilation and sampling, explicitly praising 'clearly described' experimental design and 'well-defined dataset.'

Strong agreement on claims C74-C76 regarding methodological trade-offs and data quality. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses C72-C76, noting lack of quantitative efficiency comparison and speculative nature of IgFold criticism. Peer reviewers address C74-C76, praising transparency and data availability without questioning efficiency claims or IgFold criticism.
